answer: Hypothesis (data-grounded, from the supplied dataset): In ML-enabled system projects, the two least-used documentation formats for requirements are BDD scenarios and ML Canvas. After excluding the 82 respondents who skipped the documentation question (all 'Suspended' survey participants), n=194 valid respondents answered the multi-select documentation question (Q10). BDD scenarios were quoted by only 4 of 194 respondents (2.062%, bootstrap 95% CI [0.515, 4.124]; BCa [0.000, 3.608]; Wilson [0.805, 5.181]), and the ML Canvas by 15 of 194 (7.732%, bootstrap 95% CI [4.124, 11.856]; BCa [3.608, 10.825]; Wilson [4.741, 12.364]) — the two lowest usage rates among the eleven standard documentation formats. Note the free-text 'Others' fallback option was quoted by the same 15 respondents (7.732%); it ties ML Canvas exactly but is not a standard named format, so ML Canvas is reported as the second-least-used format. The remaining formats were used far more often: Vision Document 14.948%, Goal Models 14.948%, Data Models 17.526%, Use Case Models 19.588%, Prototypes 21.649%, Requirements Lists 26.289%, User Stories 32.474%, Notebooks 34.021% ('Not_Documented', the 'no documentation' option, sat at 15.464% and is not a format). These self-computed figures from the supplied CSV (percentile bootstrap, B=10,000, seed=42, resampling respondents) differ from the 10.13% [9.926, 10.333] and 4.366% [4.231, 4.501] quoted in the question, which evidently come from a different denominator/cleaning convention (e.g., the original paper's cleaned sample); the ranking of the two least-used formats is unchanged under either convention.

payload.hypothesis: The two least-used documentation formats for requirements in ML-enabled system projects are BDD scenarios (2.062%, 95% CI [0.515, 4.124]) and ML Canvas (7.732%, 95% CI [4.124, 11.856]), i.e., 4/194 and 15/194 of the 194 respondents who answered the multi-select Q10 documentation question quoted them; the free-text 'Others' option ties ML Canvas at 7.732% but is not a standard format. Self-computed from the supplied CSV (percentile bootstrap, B=10,000, seed=42, respondent-level resampling); the question's 10.13% [9.926, 10.333] and 4.366% [4.231, 4.501] reflect a different denominator/cleaning convention, but the two least-used formats are the same.
payload.workflow: 1) Load CSV (276×202); 2) Identify Q10_ML_Documentation_* format columns (12 non-free); 3) Verify encoding {'quoted','not quoted','-77'} and that the 82 '-77' rows are identical across all columns and correspond to 'Suspended (22)' respondents; 4) Drop them → n=194; 5) Per-format usage rate = share 'quoted'; 6) Bootstrap: resample 194 respondent rows with replacement, B=10,000, seed=42, percentile 95% CI (primary), manual BCa and Wilson as checks; 7) Rank ascending; 8) Select lowest two standard formats, disclose MLCanvas/Others tie; 9) Write analysis.py and q10_format_usage_ranking.csv.
